analysis.title: Verisk Analytics Inc. (VRSK): Strong 3Q returns organic revenue growth to medium-term range, supported by subscription durability
key_insights: Verisk's 3Q 2026 results beat GS and FactSet consensus on revenue, EBITDA margin and adjusted EPS, and management reiterated full year 2026 guidance. GS maintains Neutral.

Organic constant currency (OCC) revenue growth returned to 7.4% y/y, inside the company's 6-8% medium-term target range and up from 5.8% in 2Q. GS says this raises confidence that about 8% subscription growth can sustain total revenue growth despite softer insurance markets.

Subscription revenue grew 8.2% y/y OCC and was about 84% of 3Q revenue. Drivers were forms, rules and loss costs, strong renewals, new logos in anti-fraud, pricing, client expansion and adoption of newer products such as Mozart, Forms AI Builder, Synergy Studio and digital media forensics.

Transactional revenue grew 3.2% y/y OCC after a 4.2% decline in 2Q. The gain came partly from stronger Life Solutions services revenue and data-pull overages, which VRSK does not expect to repeat in 4Q. Below-average weather activity and softer US and Canadian property markets remain headwinds.

Transactional pressure could persist into early 2027. Contractors and adjusters are about 10% of revenue, and weak weather-related demand is causing collection pressure and a small number of customer bankruptcies.

AI is described as a revenue opportunity through direct product licenses, stronger core pricing and possible separate MCP charges. Core Lines Reimagined is on track for 25 new modules in 2026, and MCP access will be extended to more applications and datasets. A customer that tried AI on its own data for fraud detection returned under a multi-year agreement after VRSK's industry-wide data gave better results.

AI-related enterprise deals face longer sales cycles because of testing around reliability, regulation, governance and contributory data. Smaller and mid-sized customers adopt AI licenses faster, and VRSK expects adoption to broaden over 12-24 months, so the timing of a 2027 contribution is uncertain.

GS flags a longer-term risk that customers consume VRSK data through APIs, MCP connectors and their own analytics tools. That would reduce the value of dashboard and workflow products, while data and models tied to the contributory datasets are more defensible.
Productivity gains from AI (FAST Studio) support reinvestment and annual margin expansion within the 25-75 bps medium-term target.

GS cut its 12-month price target to $228 from $235 (price $211.47, upside 7.8%) on a lower target multiple of 23.5x versus 25.0x prior, applied to NTM+1YR EPS of $9.71. The cut reflects less near-term visibility into transactional revenue growth.

GS estimates are largely unchanged: 2026/2027/2028 revenue $3,214mn/$3,423mn/$3,646mn and EPS $7.70/$8.79/$10.01. 4Q 2026E revenue is trimmed to $816.3mn from $820.2mn and 4Q adjusted EPS to $1.94 from $1.96.

market_movers.rationale: GS lowered its price target from $235 to $228 on a lower 23.5x target multiple (25.0x prior), citing less visibility into transactional revenue growth. The Neutral rating is maintained after a 3Q beat.

earnings_insights: VRSK 3Q 2026 (reported 11/5/2026 per the report date): revenue $809mn, +5.3% y/y, versus GS forecast 4.3% and FactSet consensus 4.9%. Exhibit 1 shows a GS revenue estimate of $801.2mn.
3Q OCC revenue growth 7.4% y/y versus GS forecast 6.5% and consensus 6.8%, accelerating from 5.8% in 2Q. Underwriting +7.7% y/y OCC, claims +6.7%.
3Q adjusted EBITDA margin 56.7% (+90 bps y/y) versus GS estimate 56.2% and consensus 56.3%, driven by operating leverage. Adjusted EBITDA $459.0mn versus GS estimate $450.0mn.

3Q adjusted EPS $1.96 (reported, adjusted basis) versus consensus $1.92 and GS $1.92 in Exhibit 1, up 14.1% from $1.72 a year earlier. GAAP EPS attributable to Verisk was $1.70 versus GS estimate $1.83.

Full year 2026 company guidance reiterated: revenue $3,190-3,240mn, adjusted EBITDA $1,790-1,830mn at 56.0-56.5% margin, EPS $7.45-7.75. GS says this points to stable consensus for revenue and margin and modest negative EPS revisions.
Pre-print 2026 estimates for comparison: GS revenue $3,210mn, EBITDA $1,808mn (56.3% margin), EPS $7.68, versus FactSet consensus revenue $3,219mn, EBITDA $1,814mn (56.4% margin), EPS $7.71.
Post-print GS estimates: 2026E/2027E/2028E EPS $7.70/$8.79/$10.01 (previously $7.68/$8.80/$9.97) and EBITDA margin 56.3%/56.9%/57.4% (unchanged).
risk_factors: Transactional revenue volatility, including below-average weather activity and softer US and Canadian property markets.
Customer bankruptcies among contractors and adjusters, a small modest headwind that could last into early 2027.
Longer enterprise sales cycles delaying conversion of AI engagement into revenue, with uncertain timing of the 2027 contribution.
AI shifting the customer interface to third-party platforms and reducing the value of dashboard and workflow products.
Macro headwinds, a deceleration in insurance premium growth and carrier spending cuts as carriers focus on profitability.

tension_points.theme: verisk subscription growth vs transactional drag
tension_points.bull_case: Subscription revenue grew 8.2% y/y OCC and is about 84% of revenue, supported by pricing, client expansion, new logos and AI monetization through direct licenses and possible MCP charges. Transactional revenue turned positive at +3.2%, and normal weather and property activity would add upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Part of the 3Q transactional gain came from Life Solutions services and data-pull overages that VRSK does not expect to repeat in 4Q. Weak weather volumes, softer property markets, customer bankruptcies and longer AI sales cycles limit visibility, and GS cut its target multiple for that reason.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Transactional pressure persisting into early 2027 and AI adoption not broadening over the next 12-24 months, which would leave the 2027 contribution from AI unrealized.

theme_stances.key_argument: Durable subscription growth supported by pricing, client expansion, new logos and newer products should sustain organic growth within the 6-8% target range.
theme_stances.evidence: Durable subscription growth should remain the primary driver

theme_stances.key_argument: AI adds revenue through direct licenses and stronger core pricing, and the contributory data supports a durable moat.
theme_stances.evidence: AI provides incremental revenue opportunities through direct licenses

theme_stances.key_argument: Weather-related volumes and softer property markets keep transactional activity under pressure, which limits near-term visibility.
